name: CanvasSceneHost
purpose: Provide a unified lifecycle host for canvas-family surfaces: mount, update, resize, theme sync, overlay slots, disposal, and diagnostics hooks.
why: Today the host lifecycle is duplicated across CanvasWorkbench, CanvasCalendar, and legacy wrappers. A dedicated host contract reduces interop drift and gives every canvas runtime the same mounting discipline.

name: SceneNodeModel
purpose: Define the internal scene graph contract used by shared graph components: nodes, children, bounds, transforms, visibility, hit regions, and state flags.
why: The current workbench contracts describe surface DTOs but not a reusable scene graph. A formal node model is needed to stop page-level graph projection and ad hoc render bookkeeping.

name: LayerStack
purpose: Model explicit rendering layers for background, connectors, node cards, overlays, selection tools, diagnostics, and accessibility mirrors.
why: The current workbench JS has implicit layers inside one DOM/SVG runtime. Explicit layering is required for predictable z-order, event routing, and performance tuning.

name: GridBackdrop
purpose: Render the shared grid, ruler cues, and spatial backdrop for graph-like canvas surfaces.
why: The current experience has spatial framing but no formal shared grid component that can support snapping, guides, zoom scaling, or future minimap rendering.

name: InvalidationScheduler
purpose: Centralize redraw invalidation, requestAnimationFrame batching, dirty-region coalescing, and state publish throttling.
why: The current runtime has local debounce helpers but no explicit invalidation model. This is the biggest architectural gap versus a healthy long-term canvas framework.

name: LayoutEngine
purpose: Own node placement resolution, DOM measurement feedback, lane positioning, group-frame bounds, and collision-aware layout helpers.
why: Layout logic exists today but is embedded in one JS file and page-specific placement code. It needs to become a first-class shared service.

name: TextMeasureService
purpose: Provide shared text measurement, wrapping, truncation, ellipsis, multi-line sizing, and font-cache behavior for graph and calendar surfaces.
why: Text is a central element of every current canvas surface, but measurement rules live implicitly in DOM or specialized JS code. A shared service is required for consistent card sizing and truncation behavior.

name: CanvasThemeTokenPack
purpose: Centralize canvas/workbench theme tokens for color, spacing, radii, shadows, line weights, typography, and dark/light readiness.
why: The current look is mostly encoded in a large CSS file and specialized widget styles. A formal token pack is needed for long-term consistency and skinning.

name: JsInteropBridge
purpose: Define a stable, modular JS bridge contract for graph and calendar runtimes without leaking page-specific helpers into shared files.
why: Interop exists today but is monolithic and mixed with Prompt Factory helper code. A bridge layer is needed to modularize runtimes and keep C# contracts explicit.

name: SerializationPersistencePack
purpose: Normalize serializable scene state, viewport state, selection state, and UI-state persistence contracts across graph and calendar surfaces.
why: State is persisted today, but schemas differ by page and are sometimes parsed manually. A shared persistence pack is essential for undo/redo, import/export, and migration safety.

name: CommandHistoryStore
purpose: Provide a shared undo/redo-ready history abstraction for editor state snapshots or domain commands.
why: Prompt Factory already has a page-local snapshot history. Project Structure and future canvases need the same capability without duplicating history stacks.

name: DiagnosticsOverlay
purpose: Surface debug information for scene bounds, layer order, hit regions, selection, frame timing, and invalidation reasons.
why: The current system has no formal debug or profiling hooks, making performance and correctness issues harder to inspect.

name: TextBlockPrimitive
purpose: Render text blocks with shared typography, line clamping, wrapping, ellipsis, alignment, and emphasis states.
why: Node cards, menus, chips, and calendar events all render text but not through one reusable primitive.

name: IconGlyphPrimitive
purpose: Render small icon glyphs, state icons, and symbolic markers with unified sizing and alignment rules.
why: Icons are currently embedded ad hoc in cards, chips, and menu entries instead of being a shared primitive.

name: ChipBadgePrimitive
purpose: Render compact chips, badges, tags, and pill indicators with consistent styling and optional icon/text composition.
why: CanvasWorkbenchChip exists as data but not as a reusable rendering primitive across all surfaces.

name: ImagePrimitive
purpose: Render images and media thumbnails with fit modes, placeholder state, error state, and progressive loading behavior.
why: Image usage exists in node cards and inspectors, but no shared canvas-friendly image primitive exists yet.

name: ContainerPrimitive
purpose: Provide a reusable container card/panel surface with padding, elevation, selection styling, clipping, and child layout slots.
why: Node cards, inspector panels, selection frames, and future popovers all need consistent container rules beyond raw HTML divs.

name: ConnectorPathPrimitive
purpose: Render connector lines, arrows, relationship paths, and route decorations between nodes or time blocks.
why: Connectors are central to both graph canvases, but rendering and routing are embedded in the shared JS file and legacy workbench runtime instead of a dedicated primitive.

name: ViewportController
purpose: Own zoom, pan, focus, fit-to-view, clamping, and coordinate conversion between scene and host space.
why: Viewport behavior exists today but is embedded inside the JS runtime and exposed piecemeal through host methods.

name: HitTestService
purpose: Provide explicit hit testing for nodes, connectors, group frames, handles, and overlay targets.
why: Hit logic exists implicitly via DOM events in the shared runtime and manually in the legacy workbench canvas; it should be unified and testable.

name: SelectionModel
purpose: Own single-select, multi-select, primary selection, range semantics, and selection-state publication.
why: Selection state is already central but split across JS state, C# DTOs, and page-level logic. It needs a shared authoritative model.

name: HoverFocusRouter
purpose: Coordinate hover, focus, and active-target visuals across nodes, connectors, menus, and editor overlays.
why: Hover and focus are currently handled locally by DOM events and CSS. A shared router is needed to keep complex overlays and keyboard interactions coherent.

name: DragDropController
purpose: Centralize pointer capture, drag start heuristics, multi-node move, group-frame move, drop targets, and drag lifecycle events.
why: Drag logic exists but is embedded in the shared runtime and page-specific move persistence. It needs clearer ownership and drop-target extensibility.

name: SnapGuideSystem
purpose: Calculate snapping candidates, alignment guides, and near-edge/center snapping behavior during move and resize operations.
why: Snapping and alignment guides are explicitly needed for future features but absent from the current implementation.

name: MarqueeSelectionOverlay
purpose: Render and manage the marquee selection rectangle and intersection query for multi-selection.
why: Marquee selection already exists in the shared runtime but is not isolated as a reusable overlay component with explicit policy knobs.

name: TransformHandlesOverlay
purpose: Render resize, rotate, and move handles around selected objects or groups.
why: Transform handles are not present today but are an expected next-step capability for richer editors and image/media nodes.

name: ConnectorAnchorOverlay
purpose: Show connector anchor points, connection affordances, and routing handles on selected or hovered nodes.
why: Future connector authoring and routing improvements need explicit anchor visuals and hit regions, which do not exist yet.

name: KeyboardShortcutRouter
purpose: Standardize canvas keyboard shortcuts, scope management, and conflict handling across graph and calendar surfaces.
why: Prompt Factory already registers custom shortcuts while the workbench runtime also handles zoom/help keys. This should be formalized.

name: ClipboardBridge
purpose: Enable copy, cut, paste, duplicate, and clipboard-serialization scenarios for selected canvas entities.
why: Clipboard workflows are called out as a requirement and are currently unsupported by shared canvas components.

name: AccessibilityMirrorLayer
purpose: Maintain a hidden but semantic DOM representation of interactive canvas content for screen readers and keyboard navigation fallbacks.
why: Canvas-heavy editors need deliberate accessibility fallback strategies; none are formalized today.

name: AnimationTimeline
purpose: Provide a minimal shared animation system for smooth transitions, focus pans, hover fades, and connector or badge micro-animations.
why: The product wants wow effect and fluidity, but there is no shared animation layer. Without one, every new animation will become bespoke.

name: CanvasWorkbenchShell
purpose: Primary reusable graph-workbench component that hosts the graph runtime, toolbar affordances, zoom rail, and typed events.
why: This already exists and is the correct strategic starting point, but it needs internal decomposition so it can become the long-lived shell of the graph framework.

name: CanvasWorkbenchStageShell
purpose: Shared stage layout that wraps the canvas shell with eyebrow/title copy, stats, inspector area, and supporting panel zones.
why: This stage shell already unifies page composition language between Project Structure and Prompt Factory.

name: NodeCardComposer
purpose: Compose graph node cards from primitives: container, text, chips, icons, image slots, metadata stacks, and inline affordances.
why: Node rendering is currently hardwired inside the shared JS runtime and page data mappers. It should become a reusable component composition layer.

name: GroupFrameOverlay
purpose: Render group frames, selection borders, logical swimlanes, and future grouping containers around sets of nodes.
why: Group frames exist already as data and JS rendering, but their generation and persistence are partly page-specific.

name: CreateActionPalette
purpose: Present quick-create actions, grouped create menus, and contextual create composers using shared action metadata.
why: Create flows are central to both canvases and already partially shared through CanvasWorkbenchAction, but rendering and orchestration are still mixed with context menus and page logic.

name: ContextMenuHost
purpose: Own context-menu placement, nested menus, keyboard dismissal, focus handling, and action dispatch.
why: A robust context menu exists in the workbench JS, but it is still embedded and mixed with create flow behaviors. It should be elevated into a reusable overlay component.

name: TooltipPopoverHost
purpose: Provide unified tooltip and popover behavior for truncated text, validation messages, inline helpers, and contextual rich previews.
why: Tooltip/popover support is explicitly missing in broader shared UI docs and is needed by upcoming canvas features.

name: InlineEditorComposer
purpose: Host lightweight inline editors for notes, labels, small property changes, and future quick edits inside the canvas stage.
why: The workbench already contains inline note composers and edit flows, but they are hardwired inside JS. They should become a reusable editor host.

name: FloatingInspectorHost
purpose: Support detachable or floating inspector presentation anchored to the canvas stage.
why: Prompt Factory already has a floating inspector helper, but it is mixed into generic workbench JS and should become a first-class shared component.

name: EmptyStateOverlay
purpose: Render meaningful empty-state overlays when a canvas surface has no content or no valid projection.
why: Empty surfaces will become more common as framework reuse grows; explicit empty-state handling is currently missing.

name: SkeletonStateOverlay
purpose: Provide loading skeletons for workbench cards, toolbar chrome, and inspector placeholders before real scene data arrives.
why: Canvas surfaces often show data-dependent content, but there is no shared skeleton strategy for them today.

name: MinimapOverview
purpose: Provide a minimap/overview of large graph scenes with viewport rectangle and quick navigation.
why: Large scenes in Project Structure and Prompt Factory will become harder to navigate without an overview. The current framework has no such component.

name: CanvasCalendarHost
purpose: Primary reusable Blazor component that hosts the calendar runtime with typed event/save/delete/export callbacks.
why: This wrapper already exists and should remain the migration target, but it needs clearer decomposition and shared host conventions.

name: CalendarTimeGridRenderer
purpose: Specialized renderer for timed/day/week calendar grids, event blocks, all-day regions, and time-axis interactions.
why: Timed-view rendering exists inside the monolithic calendar JS runtime but is not isolated for maintenance or targeted QA.

name: CalendarMiniMonthNavigator
purpose: Provide the mini-month or small navigation calendar used to jump between dates and scopes.
why: This behavior exists inside the monolithic calendar runtime and should be named explicitly for customization and testing.

name: CalendarSelectionPanel
purpose: Present selected event details, contextual playlists/checklists, and selection-derived actions in the calendar shell.
why: The calendar engine already renders supporting panels, but their responsibilities are opaque and should become explicit wrapper-level concepts.

name: CalendarEventEditorModal
purpose: Encapsulate event create/edit modal behavior, validation, and typed save/delete flows in the calendar subsystem.
why: The editor exists inside the monolithic JS engine but should be treated as a named component for lifecycle, validation, and eventual reuse.

name: CalendarCrudBridge
purpose: Bridge save, delete, playlist search/mutation, and export operations between the JS calendar widget and C# services.
why: CRUD interop exists but should be explicitly owned as a bridge component to avoid spreading calendar operation details across the wrapper.

name: CalendarExportMenu
purpose: Present export options and package visible calendar data/context into typed export requests.
why: Export is already part of the calendar contract, but the export interaction is still buried inside the widget runtime.

name: ProjectCalendarAdapter
purpose: Map project-specific calendar domain models and view-state persistence to the shared CanvasCalendar contract.
why: ProjectCalendarPage still uses a legacy wrapper and string parsing. A dedicated adapter is required to finish the migration cleanly.

name: ProjectStructureGraphAdapter
purpose: Project ProjectStructureNode/Link domain models into the shared graph scene contract used by CanvasWorkbench.
why: Project Structure mapping exists today in the page itself. A dedicated adapter is necessary to remove page-level scene construction and make the graph reusable.

name: ProjectStructureActionCatalogAdapter
purpose: Encapsulate Project Structure create/action catalog generation and adaptation to shared action metadata.
why: ProjectStructureCanvasCatalog is already a strong step toward reuse, but it should be formalized as a domain adapter that feeds shared create/action components.

name: ProjectStructurePlacementPolicy
purpose: Centralize placement rules for newly created project nodes relative to source node, parent node, viewport, and layout heuristics.
why: ResolveCreatePlacement currently lives inside the page, making future placement behavior harder to reuse or validate.

name: ProjectStructureValidationOverlay
purpose: Render project-specific validation warnings, graph health indicators, and dependency issues directly on the canvas.
why: The page already surfaces graph health information, but future richer authoring needs a first-class overlay instead of inspector-only messaging.

name: PromptFactorySessionGraphAdapter
purpose: Project Prompt Factory editor/session state into shared graph nodes, links, groups, and selection metadata.
why: Prompt Factory graph construction is still in the page. An adapter is required to make the session graph explicit and reusable.

name: PromptFactoryCatalogToolbox
purpose: Encapsulate Prompt Factory context/create action catalogs and expose them to shared create/action UI components.
why: PromptFactoryCanvasCatalog is already the seed of a domain toolbox but should be treated as a first-class adapter component.

name: PromptRunBranchLane
purpose: Represent and render branch lanes or grouped prompt-run paths within the shared graph workbench.
why: Prompt Factory already uses branch-specific layout ideas, but they are not formalized as a reusable lane component.

name: PromptSessionAttachmentNode
purpose: Shared card variant and adapter logic for attachment/media nodes inside the prompt session graph.
why: Attachment summaries already exist in the domain model, but canvas rendering is page-specific and lacks a reusable component definition.

name: PromptFactoryUndoRedoAdapter
purpose: Integrate Prompt Factory editing operations with the shared CommandHistoryStore and shortcut system.
why: Undo/redo exists but is isolated inside the page. It should become a domain adapter that plugs into shared history infrastructure.

name: RecommendationOverlay
purpose: Display AI-driven or rules-driven recommendations directly on the Prompt Factory canvas as contextual badges, callouts, or action popovers.
why: PromptFactoryService already exposes recommendation-related behavior, and future roadmap items will likely require in-canvas recommendation UX.

name: ProjectCalendarStateParser
purpose: Parse and normalize persisted project calendar view state into a typed model, replacing manual JSON probing in the page.
why: ProjectCalendarPage currently uses TryReadSelectedEventId over raw JSON. That is brittle and should be replaced by a typed parser/policy.
